clue.text: Female not just for amusement

parts.note: something not just is unfair

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a woman is treated unjustly merely for entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling fair of rides and stalls is a place of popular entertainment, so the word stands for amusement in that sense.

clue.text: Demolish Apt 10

parts.note: apt is the estate-agent abbreviation for apartment, i.e. a flat
10 is the number ten written out

explanation.surface: An order to knock down apartment number ten.
explanation.definitionFit: To level a building to the ground is to knock it down completely.

clue.text: Careless, but surprisingly gentle in 16

indicators.note: a surprising change signals that these letters are rearranged into something unexpected

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the answer to clue 16 can be read as 'gate's head', the head of the word gate, which is its first letter G

explanation.surface: Someone is remarkably mild and slapdash in a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is a joke: 16-down is GATESHEAD, read as 'gate's head', the first letter G. That G joins GENTLE and IN as fodder for 'surprisingly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Neglectful behaviour shows a lack of proper care, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Gear change takes energy: go along with that

indicators.note: a change to the word gear signals that its letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A mechanic says a gearshift needs power, and the listener concurs.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur with a statement is to accept it, which is what going along with it means.

clue.text: Turned up with roses, true to form

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new form, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A flower arrangement is said to be upturned and faithful to type.
explanation.definitionFit: A retroussé nose is one that is turned up at the tip, a borrowing from French.

clue.text: Fish happening to be around becomes obvious

indicators.note: around tells us the happening surrounds the fish

parts.note: a happening is an event
the ide or id is a freshwater fish, and ID is a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A fish turns up at some occasion and becomes plain to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evident is plainly seen, a straight synonym of obvious.

clue.text: Relieved when beheading stopped

indicators.note: beheading means the first letter is cut off the word for stopped

parts.note: to cease is to stop, so stopped gives ceased

explanation.surface: Someone felt better once the executions came to a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain that has been relieved has been eased, a direct synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Fashionable lot circulating at university to inspire foolish passion

parts.note: something fashionable is in

indicators.note: circulating means going round, so the lot surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trendy crowd moving round a campus stirs up silly crushes.
explanation.definitionFit: To infatuate someone is to make them besotted, filling them with a foolish passion.

clue.text: Peter rises when Flynn appears on screen

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: Peter Lorre was a Hollywood character actor

explanation.surface: One actor stands up whenever another film star appears on the screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears on screen' is surface colour supporting the film-actor theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Errol Flynn was the swashbuckling Hollywood star, so the surname Flynn points to his first name.

clue.text: Disloyalty evinced by one star

indicators.note: evinced by means shown by, the letters of the phrase displaying the answer in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Betrayal is exposed by a single celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is betrayal of one's country, the gravest form of disloyalty.

clue.text: Predict the game's return a month earlier

indicators.note: earlier means the month is placed before the rest

parts.note: Aug is the abbreviation for August

indicators.note: return means the abbreviation for the game is read backwards

parts.note: RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: Someone forecasts that a match will be back a month sooner.
explanation.definitionFit: To augur is to foretell, from the Roman priests who read omens.

clue.text: Time to request church to provide a working party

parts.note: to request something is to ask for it
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: It is the moment to ask the church to supply a group of volunteers.
explanation.definitionFit: A task force is a group formed for a specific job, much like a working party.

clue.text: Repeats the old favourites?

parts.note: stories told a second time are repeats of old favourites, also the title of a Hawthorne collection

explanation.surface: A complaint that the broadcaster is rerunning well-loved programmes.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is also the title of Nathaniel Hawthorne's 1837 short-story collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Stories told for a second time are retellings of familiar favourites, which the phrase describes literally.

clue.text: Wants to be interviewed back in Germany

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for Germany goes inside
back means the whole assembled piece is read in reverse

parts.note: a patient or applicant who has been interviewed has been seen
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to get a job interview on returning to Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: To need something is to want it, both as verbs in the third person.

clue.text: Homicidal maniac, alien about 50

indicators.note: about means the word for alien goes round the numeral

parts.note: an alien is a stranger
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A murderer is described as a foreigner of around fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: A strangler is a killer who throttles victims, a kind of homicidal maniac.

clue.text: Good northern woman caught in wrongdoing by railway worker

indicators.note: caught in tells us the first pieces sit inside the word for wrongdoing

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing
Alma is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A decent northern lady is caught misbehaving by a man working on the railways.
explanation.definitionFit: A signalman operates railway signals, so he is a railway worker.

clue.text: Obstacles chap overcomes this time in Tyneside

indicators.note: in a down clue, overcomes means the chap sits on top of what follows

parts.note: gates are barriers, obstacles to passage
he is a male person, a chap
AD, anno Domini, marks the present era

explanation.surface: Barriers that a man gets over at this moment somewhere in north-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the urban area along the River Tyne in north-east England; Gateshead lies on its south bank, opposite Newcastle.
explanation.definitionFit: Gateshead is a town that forms part of Tyneside, so the clue defines by location.

clue.text: Goldfish placed in the old lady's tomb

indicators.note: placed in means the gold and fish go inside the word for the old lady

parts.note: one's old lady is one's mother, mum
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
the sole is a flatfish

explanation.surface: A goldfish is put in mother's grave.
explanation.definitionFit: A mausoleum is a grand building housing a tomb, so it stands for one.

clue.text: Get rented accommodation for cleaner

indicators.note: accommodation suggests an adjusted arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Find a rented flat for the cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A detergent is a cleansing agent, so it is a cleaner in the substance sense.

clue.text: Held up accursed release

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means the word reads upwards, so it is reversed

parts.note: someone accursed is reviled, condemned

explanation.surface: A damned man's freedom was delayed.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver someone is to set them free, a synonym of release as a verb.

clue.text: Furnish an English witticism

parts.note: a quip is a witticism

explanation.surface: Someone supplies an Englishman's clever remark.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip is to provide with what is needed, the same as to furnish.

clue.text: Right chirpy about such a victory?

indicators.note: about signals the letters are turned around and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether one is perfectly cheerful about a triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: The irony is the point: a Pyrrhic victory costs so much it is hardly worth being chirpy about.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pyrrhic victory is one won at ruinous cost, so the word describes such a win.

clue.text: Burdened man clutching poster

indicators.note: clutching means the man's name holds the poster inside

parts.note: Len is a man's name
an ad, short for advertisement, is a poster

explanation.surface: A weighed-down man grips an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means loaded, carrying a heavy burden.

clue.text: Oooo! Sweetheart!

definitions.meaning: a duck is a cricket score of nought, so four noughts are a set of them
a northern British term of endearment, like love or dear

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise and affection.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter out for nought scores a duck, so a row of Os is several of them; 'ducks' is also everyday British slang for dear.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both zero scores in cricket and a friendly endearment.

clue.text: Duke is taking time about working. Shame!

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means the time word goes round the word for working

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A nobleman spends ages at his job, and it is a disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonour is disgrace or loss of reputation, a synonym of shame.

clue.text: Navigator died a roué

parts.note: a roué is a rake, a dissolute man

explanation.surface: A seafarer died a womaniser.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis Drake was the Elizabethan navigator who circled the globe.

clue.text: Scrap over dramatist

parts.note: an ort is a scrap of food left over
on can mean upon, over

explanation.surface: A row breaks out about a playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Orton was the English playwright of Loot and Entertaining Mr Sloane.

clue.text: Sit on the fence if Bill's in house with Lawrence

indicators.note: in means the bill goes inside the house

parts.note: a villa is a house
AC, account, is a bill
T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, gives his initials

explanation.surface: Wondering whether to stay neutral if Bill lives with Lawrence.
explanation.definitionFit: To vacillate is to waver between options, which is sitting on the fence.

clue.text: Effectiveness can make a firm impression

definitions.meaning: a law with ... has real force, so the word means effectiveness
what bites leaves a clear impression, as in dental marks

explanation.surface: Power to act leaves a lasting mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means real force or power and also the biting parts that leave marks.

clue.text: Standoffishness put aside

definitions.meaning: to keep it aside for later

explanation.surface: Aloofness kept apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means aloofness of manner and the verb means to keep something back.

clue.text: Energetic sleuths catch a good few going west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left, so the whole is reversed
catch means the sleuths hold the other piece inside

parts.note: the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives
a good few means many

explanation.surface: Lively detectives arrest quite a lot of people heading westwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamic means full of energy and drive, a synonym of energetic.
